transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-02 16:00 PDT
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Alice Monroe (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Rivera (Redwood CSM - 10m), Priya Kapoor (CTO, ThresholdAI), Jamal Chen (Head of Infra), Marta Lopez (SRE), Victor (PM)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on Dedicated (reserved GPU) fit: isolation requirements, burst/warmpool strategy, target latency SLAs, and compliance/KMS path for Private deployment. Customer evaluating Redwood vs MegaAI Cloud for predictable cost and lower tail-latency on their multi-model mix (Llama3 and a proprietary 20B fine-tune).

Topics covered:
- Current infra and pain: noisy neighbors on shared GPUs, unpredictable p99 latency spikes during model-heavy jobs
- Model mix and sizing: mix of 13B/20B/70B (open + internal), mostly quantized; expect steady baseline plus intermittent spikes from product features
- Desired SLOs: p95 150ms gen (short completion tasks), p99 under 800ms for interactive flows, bulk batch embeddings less strict
- Isolation: need single-tenant allocation for PII-sensitive workloads, RBAC and audit logs required
- Burst strategy: warm pool vs pre-warmed hotnodes vs burst credits; fallback model variants for graceful degradation
- Compliance/KMS: SOC 2, encryption at rest, KMS/HSM integration for Private deployment path

Transcript body (timestamps approximate):
[00:00] Alice (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for doing this, quick intros?
[00:05] Priya (CTO): Hi, Priya here, CTO at ThresholdAI. We're looking at reserved capacity options, trying to understand if Redwood Dedicated or Private is better for us.
[00:12] Jamal (Infra): Jamal, infra. We've been hit by noisy neighbor p99 spikes on our current managed endpoints.
[00:20] Samir (SE): Yep, we'll dig into that; curious on model mix and what your baseline vs peaks look like.
[00:25] Victor (PM): Victor, product. We have two new features that can cause bursty inference—document QA and a low-latency chat.

[02:10] Samir (SE): Can you walk through typical traffic profile? like RPS and which models for each flow?
[02:18] Priya: Sure, baseline about 120 rps across endpoints, but 95th percentile windows go to 900 rps for short durations—usually 5 to 20 minutes, sometimes longer during launches. Model mix: 60% 13B Llama variants (q8_0), 30% our internal 20B fine-tune (q4_0), 10% occasional 70B for long-form synthesis, that's heavy and rare. We also run nightly batch embedding jobs.
[03:01] Samir: OK, so baseline steady plus high short spikes. For Dedicated, we can reserve a pool that covers your baseline and then burst out to hot pool. Do you have a strict isolation / tenancy requirement for all models?
[03:15] Jamal: For the 20B model we want single-tenant, because of training data with customer PII. 13B open models can be multi-tenant, we're fine there.
[03:28] Marta (SRE): Also need audit logs for inference requests and KMS-based keying for any model outputs that touch customer data.

[05:00] Samir: That's doable. For Dedicated we offer reserved GPU pools (A100/H100 options) with tenant fencing so your nodes aren't shared. We can also present a Private path where the control plane is in your VPC for full KMS/HSM integration and on-prem if needed.
[05:24] Priya: What's the typical latency delta between Hosted and Dedicated? We care about p99 tail.
[05:33] Samir: On our benchmarks, Dedicated with pinned nodes and warm pool shows much tighter tail — p99 reductions of 30-60% compared to noisy shared endpoints, depends on model and packing. For 13B quantized we often see p95 under 100ms on H100 pinned nodes; p99 tends to be 300-500ms. For larger models like 70B it's longer of course.
[06:05] Priya: That would help. Our problem now is unpredictable p99 spikes hitting SLAs with customers.

[07:12] Victor: How do you handle bursts? Do you prewarm or spin up on demand?
[07:20] Samir: Two techniques—warm pool (a reserve of pre-warmed instances) for fast bursts, and a burst-to-hosted fallback where requests route to a compatible hosted variant if Dedicated capacity saturates. We also support a burst-credit model so you can reserve less and consume burst credits up to a cap.
[07:45] Jamal: That hosted fallback worries me; we'd prefer to keep PII-bearing requests inside the private/dedicated envelope.
[07:53] Alice: Right, so we can restrict fallbacks only to non-sensitive paths; for sensitive requests we can enforce strict routing to your private pool.

[09:40] Marta: Operationally, how do you prewarm? Is the KV cache persisted when scaling? We use long-context streaming and KV cache matters.
[09:50] Samir: We manage KV cache per-tenant; warm pool nodes retain KV cache for pinned sessions when possible, but under node churn we rehydrate. For long-lived chat you can pin sessions to hotnodes. Also note sometimes transcription: we call it KV cash in some logs, hmm — but real system's KV cache rehydration is part of the warm-path.

[11:22] Priya: Cost tradeoffs—what's the unit economics for reserved vs pure hosted? Example numbers?
[11:30] Alice: We'll send a pricing band after this call, but high level: reserved has lower per-token cost and more predictable billing because you pay for the pool; hosted is usage-based and can be cheaper for spiky but low-volume. The burst-credit program lets you keep baseline reserved at lower size and use credits for spikes, balancing cost and capacity predictability.

[13:05] Samir: Important question—what analytics do you need? You mentioned SLOs and cost breakdown by model and route?
[13:12] Priya: Yes, per-route latency, token breakdown, who called it (RBAC), and audit trail. Also we run red-team evals so we'd want easy snapshotting of outputs for quality regression.
[13:30] Samir: Redwood Console provides per-route dashboards, token-level costs and traces and eval hooks to tie quality regressions to prompt sets.

[15:10] Jamal: On encryption—KMS integration: do you support customer-managed keys in Private? And HSM optionally?
[15:18] Samir: Yes, Private includes KMS/HSM integrations with your VPC. We'll hand over the SAML/SSO and RBAC setup steps. For Dedicated (hosted control plane) we can integrate with customer KMS for data at rest on their dedicated pool via envelope encryption.

[17:03] Marta: If we pick Dedicated with warm pool, what's the typical cold start for a large (70B) model?
[17:10] Samir: Cold start depends — loading 70B weights can take tens of seconds to a minute if not prewarmed; our hotnodes typically pre-warm for mission-critical flows. For 13B/20B quantized it's sub-second to a few seconds depending on checkpoint and KV rehydration.

[19:00] Victor: Do you support model variants for graceful degradation? e.g., fallback to a smaller quantized model if hot path saturated?
[19:08] Samir: Yes, policy-based routing allows you to fall back to compatible model variants — we can configure canary, A/B, or degrade to a faster quantized variant during spikes. This is part of our graceful degradation playbook.

[21:40] Priya: Important — we need to know eviction and preemption semantics. If our reserved pool hits host-level maintenance or failures, what's the failover?
[21:50] Samir: Reserved pools are SLA-backed, but for additional resilience we recommend a small cross-region sibling pool or setting a dedicated failover policy to burst into a private fallback in another region; hotpool warm nodes help too. We can also configure node-level affinity and anti-affinity to reduce correlated failures.

[24:00] Jamal: Any options for GPU type mix? We have some models that benefit from H100 and cheaper workloads from A100.
[24:08] Samir: Yes, Dedicated supports mixed pools; you can map model tags to hardware classes. We'll help size the initial pool split and can recommend quantization strategy to optimize cost.

[26:20] Marta: For our compliance team: audit logs must show per-token request ID, model version, and user identity. Can Redwood preserve that?
[26:29] Jules (CSM): Yes, we preserve per-request metadata, plus retention options for logs. We also can assist with SOC 2 evidence collection.

[28:50] Priya: How do you measure and guarantee SLOs? Do you provide credits for missed SLOs?
[28:57] Alice: SLA terms and uptime/latency SLOs are part of the Dedicated contract — we can offer credits under objectives for sustained violation windows. We'll include specifics in the SOW.

[31:10] Victor: Regarding burst credits—how are they consumed? Any smoothing?
[31:18] Samir: They are consumed when usage exceeds reserved baseline; we apply smoothing windows and fair use. We can also set hard caps to protect billing, and alerts when credits near exhaustion.

[33:00] Jamal: We want to run a realistic sim—can Redwood run a customer-side spike sim or do we ship telemetry and you run it?
[33:08] Samir: We can do both. Ideally you give a 48h sample of traffic + model mix and we'll replay it in our staging to measure tail behaviors; Samir: I'll run a sim with A100 and H100 mixes and send results.

[35:50] Priya: What about preemption of spot instances for scale? We currently use cloud spot for some non-critical batch — can that be used for burst?
[35:58] Samir: For mission-critical interactive, we don't recommend spot because of preemption; for large batch and embedding jobs it's fine. For interactive bursts, warm pool or reserved burst nodes are better.

[38:12] Marta: Are there tooling hooks for observability? e.g., Prometheus metrics or open telemetry traces exported to our stack?
[38:20] Samir: Yes, Redwood exposes telemetry; Console has native dashboards but we can stream metrics to your Prometheus/Grafana or forward traces to your OTLP collector.

[40:00] Alice: A couple of practical items—what's your timeline for decision and procurement constraints?
[40:06] Priya: We're aiming to decide in 3–4 weeks. Procurement needs SOC2 + data residency notes. We may start with a pilot covering baseline capacity for two months.
[40:20] Alice: Good — we'll prioritize the security docs and pricing so procurement can review.

[42:45] Victor: Any known limitations on KV cache size or multi-session pinning?
[42:52] Samir: There's configuration limits per node but we can size nodes to accommodate expected KV usage. For many simultaneous long-context sessions, we recommend more smaller instances or pinning specific sessions to hot nodes.

[45:00] Jamal: If we do Private (VPC) route, what's the onboarding duration?
[45:06] Jules (CSM): Typical Private onboarding 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals; Dedicated (hosted control plane + reserved pool) can be as fast as 2–3 weeks to get a baseline reserved pool live.

[47:30] Priya: For contract terms—do you do quarterly or annual reserved commits?
[47:35] Alice: Both, we have monthly, quarterly, and annual commitment profiles — longer commitments get better per-unit pricing and flexible burst credits.

[49:50] Victor: Any sample SOW or contract we can look at?
[49:55] Alice: Yes, I'll share a contract template and sample SOW after this call.

[51:20] Priya: Quick follow-up on routing—we want to ensure sensitive routes never leave our dedicated pool. Is that a config flag?
[51:27] Samir: Yes, it's a routing policy. We'll configure route tags and an allowlist that prevents sensitive endpoints from bursting to hosted fallback.

[53:10] Alice: OK, recap and next steps: Samir will run the 48h spike sim and Alice will send pricing and security docs. Priya/Jamal will send traffic samples. We'll reconvene after results.
[53:28] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[53:35] Jamal: Thanks.
[53:40] Alice: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.

End of transcript.

Notes / minor transcription quirks: some brand/model terms were transcribed inconsistently (e.g., H-one hundred vs H100), occasional filler words and small drops.
